name: issue-grinder
description: Deliver Task Manager scope, compose plans, and auto-review plans before launch or active long runs.

interface.shortDescription: Deliver scope; review plans before launch or active long runs.
interface.longDescription: Includes three independent Task Manager skills. Issue Grinder delivers an explicit issue, Release, Project, or current-Release scope through To Do, In Progress, and In Review. It also answers pure questions about its modes, default resolver, differences, or selection through a delivery-free help path that does not access Task Manager, create a Goal, rename the task, or call subagents. It supports five stable execution modes: Solo keeps all Issue Grinder delivery work in one execution lane on the current top-level model while allowing bounded service-provider agents outside that topology; in Classic the controller does almost all work and gives Luna only trivial, strictly bounded packets; in Balance the main agent completes admission and dispatch before any source change or long packet-local gate, counts avoidable tool-bound wait in the benefit decision, and then owns architecture, integration, and final acceptance while exactly one wave of two or three Luna High writers implements disjoint self-contained packets in parallel with useful main work, followed by one collective wait, mechanical fan-in, centrally parallel tool-bound gates, and no separate reviewer by default; in Manager, whose internal wire identifier remains Swarm, the controller creates one full-scope brief, one persistent Luna Max manager guides one persistent Luna Max implementer through large sequential phases of one candidate, one independent Luna Max reviewer checks the completed candidate without delegating descendants, and the controller performs the final gate; Economical maximizes safe progress and may leave one honest resumable checkpoint instead of claiming completion. Balance admits only dependency-ready packets with disjoint ownership, stable interfaces, local oracles, no shared external effect, and no independent architecture; if fewer than two qualify, the main agent continues sequentially. Solo works with one or many issues and is always selected by default; Classic, Balance, Manager, and Economical require an explicit user request. The decision is made once per continuous run. Mode topology includes only agents doing Issue Grinder delivery work; outer controllers and bounded semantic providers stay outside it unless they take on analysis, implementation, testing, technical review, candidate selection, or delivery decisions. It creates a strategic Goal only for an explicitly invoked multi-issue run, keeps live scope dynamic, treats blocked-by as an implementation-readiness gate, and requires human-readable comments for every non-trivial lifecycle transition. Strategic Outcome stays present during implementation, delegation, review, blocker analysis, resume, and final reflection so local decisions serve the overall purpose. It never creates hidden requirements or new task debt: the formal completion condition remains a fresh empty active Task scope, even when the broader Strategic Outcome is only partially achieved. A candidate blocker must become a causal explanation and a fresh reflection over current primary sources; any verified safe in-scope action cancels the blocker and resumes work. A terminal handoff lists every confirmed blocking cause and gives a separate answer for each one explaining why it blocks the mandatory result of an active issue, why Issue Grinder cannot resolve it alone, and what the blocked step contributes to the issue contract and overall goal. Public UAT and other confirmed non-production environments do not need routine approval, while Production remains forbidden. Independent writers and recovery candidates use separate feature branches and Git worktrees, one integration owner performs fan-in, and final acceptance applies to one exact integrated candidate. Task Composer remains planning-only and creates Task Manager Backlog scope without implementing it. It keeps Strategic Outcome, protected Human Requirements, and the mutable Agent Plan distinguishable, projects relevant strategic context into child Tasks, and never promotes an agent assumption or optional hardening into a Human Requirement. All three skills use the separately installed Task Manager adapter. In all five modes Issue Grinder uses the standalone Strategic Explainer when available and otherwise writes natively; its provider remains outside mode execution topology while it handles only publication, and Explainer absence never blocks comments, status transitions, or final reporting. Scope Reviewer turns an exact selected plan or active Release into one human-readable report through separate fresh Luna Max perspectives. Plan review and every Release review remain read-only; explicit plan-improvement intent may change only the agent-owned planning model, never Human Requirements, delivery lifecycle, or working statuses. It reports formal Task completion separately from broader strategic achievement, and a strategic gap does not create a blocker, Task, or delivery loop. It uses the standalone Strategic Explainer when available and otherwise returns its own factual report with the missing editorial pass stated honestly.
defaultPrompt: Используй $issue-grinder, чтобы довести текущий Release в Task Manager до проверенного результата
Используй $issue-grinder:task-composer, чтобы оформить это требование в Task Manager Backlog
Используй $issue-grinder:scope-reviewer для ревью плана перед запуском или понятного обзора активного долгого Release.
